reason: I'll strengthen the bone framework first. The picture shows spaces for mineral and says the mineral resists compression.
expectation: I expect the mineral to harden the existing bone framework while its living cells and joint remain.

alternatives.reason: Building the front muscle also matches a goal, but I want to strengthen the bones first.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the elbow joint movable. Now I need to build the muscles before attaching them.
reaction: It makes sense that the hard bone and flexible joint stay different.
reason: I'll build the front muscle first; its cells and supporting tissue match the muscle-building goal.
expectation: I expect the cells and supporting tissue to form a front upper-arm muscle, though I'm unsure exactly how they fit together.

alternatives.reason: The back muscle also needs building, but either side seems reasonable to start with.

effect: The front cells and supporting tissue formed the biceps, with tendon ends reaching across the elbow. I still need the back muscle.
reaction: The picture helped me see how separate cells become fibres in a whole muscle.
reason: I'll build the back muscle so both sides are ready to attach.
expectation: I expect a back upper-arm muscle with fibres and tendon ends, similar to the biceps.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the biceps now, but I'd rather build both muscles first.

effect: Both muscles are built, and the triceps picture shows its attachment behind the elbow. Now they need to be attached to the skeleton.
reaction: The matching cutaways make the two muscles easy to compare.
reason: I'll attach the biceps first, following its pictured path across the front of the elbow.
expectation: I expect the biceps to attach to the skeleton with its tendon ends across the front of the elbow.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attaching, but either muscle seems reasonable to attach first.

effect: The biceps is attached across the front of the elbow, and its pull bends the forearm. The triceps still needs attaching at the back.
reaction: The arrows make the connection between pulling and bending clear.
reason: I'll attach the triceps to complete the opposing pair; it's the only combination offered.
expectation: I expect the triceps to attach behind the elbow so its pull can help straighten the arm.

effect: The completed arm shows how muscles pulling on opposite sides bend and straighten the elbow.
reaction: The two views made the opposing pulls clear and satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Attaching the triceps was most worthwhile: the two views showed why both muscles are needed when muscles can only pull.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the back muscle felt somewhat repetitive after the similar front-muscle construction, though comparing them was useful.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the separate muscle cells to join into long fibres, with supporting tissue continuing into tendon ends.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the goals and pictures explained the parts. Choosing which muscle to build or attach first felt like a matter of order rather than a meaningful difference.

continue.text: Yes. Building the arm connected cells, tissues and movement clearly enough to make me curious about another body system.
